 OMMA clarifies which medical marijuana products are affected by recall
 State regulators say only products mixed with a batch that failed testing are included in the recall.
 Cassidy Mudd 
 October 26, 2026 08:30 PM 1 min read 
 OKLAHOMA - The Oklahoma Medical Marijuana Authority is clarifying which medical marijuana products are affected by a recall issued Tuesday, Oct. 20, after receiving questions about a batch that initially passed laboratory testing.
 The recall involves medical marijuana flower production batches from Blue Collar Criminals Collective LLC, a licensed Oklahoma grow facility.
 According to OMMA, questions arose about products from batch number BIS091326-2 following the recall announcement.
 The agency said the batch initially passed laboratory testing, but a portion was later mixed with another batch that failed testing, making the mixed products unsafe.
 Only products that were mixed with the failed batch are included in the recall. Products from batch BIS091326-2 that were not mixed are not affected.
 OMMA also recognized Blue Collar Criminals Collective LLC for quickly reporting the issue, saying the company’s actions helped prevent the distribution of potentially unsafe products.
 The agency is encouraging all licensed medical marijuana businesses to report potential product safety concerns immediately so regulators can investigate and notify the public.
 Patients and businesses can review the recall notice and affected product list on OMMA’s website .
